decision: Seek removable premium with survivable upside exposure; delta and distance describe the trade.
key_points: Documented: Pandar compared expiries, anticipated tail collapse, sized for NVDA190. No documented z-score selector or automatic call-spread conversion.
Separate ATM, call-minus-ATM, put-minus-ATM. Put buying can move risk reversal without cheapening the sold call.
Track excess depth, duration, slope and slowing expansion. Extremity alone is not exhaustion; pre-order HIRO call flow losing price impact supports it.
Distinguish broad wing, local kink and expiry bump using synchronized executable quotes; irregularity may be noise.
Reprice partial wing flattening with ATM unchanged; separately test ATM crush, no normalization and upside chase. Compare net dollars against stressed loss across strikes/expiries.

Prior independent comparable episodes’ median change, dispersion and continued-expansion frequency inform scenarios. Otherwise normalization is sensitivity, not expected return. Expanding demand favors patience or reduced exposure; stalled demand strengthens the bump-sale case.
risks: MRVL lacks forward-history support; kink unproven.
HIRO cannot establish dealer inventory; naked-call loss is unbounded.
confidence: High on interpretation and decomposition; unproven on predictive edge.
